title: Flux OCIRepository for the ESO chart needs a `layerSelector`

detection.reason: Flux OCIRepository objects are not collected

quote: If you are using Flux + OCIRepository to fetch External Secrets Operator charts, please update your object to use a Layer selector:
remediation: Add `spec.layerSelector: {mediaType: application/vnd.cncf.helm.chart.content.v1.tar+gzip, operation: extract}` to the OCIRepository that pulls `oci://ghcr.io/external-secrets/charts/external-secrets`; the chart artifacts are now built with a different layer layout.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ocirepositories.source.toolkit.fluxcd.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.url | test("external-secrets")) | select(.spec.layerSelector == null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row pulls the ESO chart without a layerSelector
coversNotes: v2.2.0 (General): fix: publish now uses docker build v4 which required some changes

title: AWS Secrets Manager PushSecret: a resource policy and tags not in metadata are removed from AWS on every reconcile

detection.reason: the store a PushSecret pushes to is a reference; the AWS-side policy and tags are not collected

quote: **Note:** ESO treats the PushSecret as the **source of truth** for tags.
remediation: For each PushSecret named that pushes to AWS Secrets Manager: (1) a resource policy attached to the secret in AWS outside ESO is DELETED whenever `metadata.spec.resourcePolicy` is unset, including on PushSecrets with no metadata at all; since 1.0 that ran when the value changed, from 2.2 it runs on every reconcile. Move the policy into `metadata.spec.resourcePolicy` or stop pushing that secret. (2) With `metadata.spec.tags`, list every tag the secret must keep; tags added in AWS outside ESO are deleted on the next reconcile, even when the value is unchanged.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pushsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterpushsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name) stores=\([(.spec.secretStoreRefs // .spec.pushSecretSpec.secretStoreRefs // [])[].name] | join(",")) policy=\(any((.spec.data // .spec.pushSecretSpec.data // [])[]; .metadata.spec.resourcePolicy != null))"'  # each row is a PushSecret, its stores and whether it sets a resourcePolicy; on an AWS Secrets Manager store policy=false means the AWS-side policy is deleted
